items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: My mother was a very, very, very wonderful person. She was from Lafayette, Louisiana. Her family name was Lefebvre.

ctx.x: My mother was a very, very, very wonderful person. She was from Lafayette, Louisiana. Her family name was

Lefebvre. This is a mixture of Negro and Indian, although I saw many blanché or fair-haired people coming up to visit us and they were kissing mother. So I would -- they was cousins or something of this sort.

My father, it seems, that I heard of him but I didn't see him until I was 50 years old and very rare occasion. It seems that my mother was working in service naturally for certain people who had the money and they fell in love or something happened there and I was created -- I happened on the scene. So as I can remember, my mother was telling me, "Your father is in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. You don't look like your father. You look like your uncle." So I kept that in mind.
